hook.label: Respiratory medicine
hook.sub: Airways, lungs, pleura and respiratory muscles
hook.say: Pulmonology, or respiratory medicine, covers the anatomy, physiology, diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the airways, the lungs, the pleura, and the respiratory muscles.

beats.label: 1 · Core physiology
beats.say: Gas exchange depends on three processes. Ventilation brings air to the alveoli. Perfusion brings blood to the pulmonary capillaries. And diffusion moves oxygen and carbon dioxide across the membrane between them.

beats.label: Ventilation · V̇
beats.big: Not all air reaches the alveoli
beats.sub: Alveolar ventilation = (tidal volume − dead space) × rate
beats.say: Ventilation is air reaching the alveoli. Of a typical {500|five hundred} millilitre breath, about {150|one hundred and fifty} fills the conducting airways, the anatomical dead space. Only about {350|three hundred and fifty} takes part in gas exchange.

beats.label: Perfusion · Q̇
beats.say: Perfusion is blood flow through the pulmonary capillaries. The lungs receive the whole output of the right ventricle, about five litres a minute, at a mean pressure of roughly {15|fifteen} millimetres of mercury, far lower than the systemic circulation.

beats.label: Diffusion
beats.sub: Fick's law: flow ∝ area × gradient ÷ thickness
beats.say: Diffusion follows Fick's law. Gas transfer rises with membrane area and the partial pressure gradient, and falls with membrane thickness. The lung offers roughly fifty to a hundred square metres, less than half a micrometre thick.

beats.label: Diffusion · timing
beats.big: Done in a third of the time
beats.sub: Capillary PO₂ equilibrates in about 0.25 s of a 0.75 s transit
beats.say: At rest, a red cell spends about {0.75|nought point seven five} seconds in the capillary. Its oxygen pressure rises from about {40|forty} to {100|one hundred} millimetres of mercury within the first third. That reserve is lost when the membrane thickens, or when transit time shortens on exercise.

beats.label: Matching · V̇/Q̇
beats.say: The three must match. Overall, about four litres of alveolar ventilation meet five litres of blood each minute, a ratio near {0.8|nought point eight}. At one extreme, perfused but unventilated alveoli form a shunt. At the other, ventilated but unperfused alveoli are dead space.

beats.label: Clinical link
beats.sub: Each process fails in recognisable ways
beats.say: Each process has its own failures. Airway obstruction and weak respiratory muscles impair ventilation. Pulmonary embolism impairs perfusion. Fibrosis thickens the membrane, and emphysema destroys its area, impairing diffusion.

outro: Ventilation, perfusion and diffusion: three processes that must work, and match, for every breath.
